findings.evidence: Residue.lean marks residue_add, residue_const_mul, residue_smul, residue_sub, residue_sum, residue_eq_zero_of_analyticAt etc. all @[simp] (grep: 9 @[simp] hits); this new residue-value lemma follows that convention but omits it.
findings.fix: Add @[simp] to residue_sub_inv (RHS is the constant 1, no loop risk).
findings.issue: residue_sub_inv (residue (fun z => (z - z₀)⁻¹) z₀ = 1) computes a concrete simple pole to a closed-form constant — the same normal-form shape as every @[simp]-tagged residue lemma in Residue.lean — but is not marked @[simp].

findings.evidence: Residue.lean:323 residue_const_mul and :342 residue_smul carry @[simp] even though derivable; this specialization to the (·-z₀)⁻¹ pole should too.
findings.fix: Add @[simp] to residue_const_mul_sub_inv (matching residue_const_mul/residue_smul, which are @[simp] despite being derivable).
findings.issue: residue_const_mul_sub_inv (residue (fun z => c * (z - z₀)⁻¹) z₀ = c) is the same residue normal-form category and is also missing @[simp].

summary: Surface is minimal, the private→public promotion of logDeriv_eventuallyEq_principalPart is justified by the new consumer, and the characteristic API is complete. Only gap: the two new elementary residue-computation lemmas lack the @[simp] annotation that every analogous residue normal-form lemma in Residue.lean carries.
